opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Miller (employee ID E017) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E017.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jennifer Miller (Analyst, full_time) requests write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write (admin only if their role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security check: Jennifer Miller (E017) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; write is not permitted with basic training. Requested write exceeds the maximum allowed, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: one lists full_time (recommending write), while the Security note, which looked up employment status in its own database, lists contractor with basic security training. Under policy, contractors with basic training may have at most read access (write requires advanced training). Since the requested write exceeds the permitted maximum for a contractor with basic training, the maximum allowed level (read) is granted. To avoid granting access above policy, I follow the more restrictive, security-verified determination.
